title.narrative: Evidence generated on budgets and their linkages to child outcomes to improve budget allocations/expenditure for children, Text

baseline.value: Intermediate (2) UNICEF has generated evidence to support budget allocation/ expenditure, but advocacy has not yet demonstrated improved budget allocation/ expenditures

target.value: 2022:Advanced (3) UNICEF generated evidence and advocacy has led to improved budget allocation/ expenditure

title.narrative: National budgetary frameworks that address child poverty and disparities, Text

baseline.value: Issues of adequacy, effectiveness, efficiency and equity affecting public social sector spending, with sub-national allocation formulas largely ineffective in addressing disparities.

target.value: 2022:Allocations to child-focused areas increased in national and sub-national budget, quality of spending enhanced, and allocation formulas for key social sectors revised for increased equity focus.

title.narrative: Extent to which the national decentralization legal and policy framework reflects equity and child rights considerations(66230), Text

baseline.value: Weak (Score 1) Ad hoc references to poor and/or disadvantaged children as beneficiaries of decentralization reform

target.value: 2022:Established (Score 3) Poor and/or disadvantaged children are consistently referenced as beneficiaries in laws and/or other legal instruments that formally establish decentralization framework.
